faqs.question: What is a "record" in RoseRocket?
faqs.shortAnswer: A record is any order, invoice, quote, or manifest you create. One-time records like customer profiles are counted once. Each record costs approximately $0.04 USD.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket uses a record-based pricing model. There are two types: one-time records (customer profiles, carrier profiles, driver profiles, assets) that are counted once when created, and recurring records (orders, invoices, quotes, manifests) that count each time you create them. Importantly, stops within an order, documents attached to orders, and status updates don't count as records. For example, if you create 1,000 orders and 1,000 invoices per month, that's 2,000 recurring records. At $0.04 per record, you can calculate your monthly cost based on your volume. This makes pricing predictable and scales with your business.

faqs.question: What are your contract terms and lengths?
faqs.shortAnswer: You start with a 3-month activation period on month-to-month billing, then move to a 12-month contract. We offer discounts for quarterly or annual upfront payment.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket's contract structure is designed to ensure successful implementation. You begin with a 3-month activation period where you're billed month-to-month with no long-term commitment. This gives both teams time to ensure the platform fits your needs. After activation, you move to a standard 12-month contract. Payment options include month-to-month (highest rate, most flexibility), quarterly (small discount, pay every 3 months), or annual (25% discount, pay upfront). The contract auto-renews annually unless you cancel with 30-day notice. This structure protects both parties while ensuring you're committed to success.

faqs.question: Are we charged during the onboarding period?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, billing starts when you get system access, but you're on month-to-month during the 3-month activation period with no long-term commitment until after onboarding completes.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Billing begins as soon as you receive access to RoseRocket because we want both teams fully committed to a successful implementation. However, during the 3-month activation period, you're on flexible month-to-month billing with no long-term contract. This ensures mutual commitment without locking you in before you've fully experienced the platform. Record usage during onboarding is typically minimal since you're primarily in training and configuration mode. Once activation completes and you're fully live, that's when the 12-month commitment begins. This model has helped us achieve higher success rates because everyone is invested from day one.

faqs.question: Can we pay in Canadian dollars?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, RoseRocket offers Canadian dollar pricing with exchange rates applied at current market rates.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Absolutely. We understand many of our Canadian customers prefer to budget and pay in CAD. We apply current market exchange rates to convert USD pricing to Canadian dollars. For example, based on recent rates, $2,033 USD monthly converts to approximately $2,846 CAD, and an $18,000 USD annual plan converts to roughly $25,616 CAD. Exchange rates are locked in at the time of contract signing, so you have predictability for your budget planning. This makes it easier for your finance team to manage subscriptions in your home currency.

faqs.question: What happens if we don't use all our allocated records?
faqs.shortAnswer: Unused records automatically roll over to the next year with no expiration, so you never lose what you've paid for.
faqs.detailedAnswer: This is one of the customer-friendly features of our pricing model. If you purchase 12,000 records annually but only use 8,000, the remaining 4,000 automatically rolls into year two. You won't be charged again until you've used those rolled-over records. There's no expiration on unused records, so you're never penalized for overestimating your volume or for having a slower period. This gives you peace of mind that you're only paying for what you actually use over time, even if usage fluctuates. Most customers find their usage stabilizes after the first year, making planning easier.

faqs.question: Is pricing all-inclusive or are there add-ons?
faqs.shortAnswer: The base price includes all core TMS features, mobile app, QuickBooks integration, standard integrations, and support. Add-ons are only for specialized integrations or custom development.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Our pricing is designed to be transparent and all-inclusive for most customers. The base subscription includes all core TMS functionality, unlimited driver users on the mobile app, QuickBooks integration, standard ELD integrations like Motive and Samsara, customer support, regular software updates, data storage, and comprehensive training materials. The only potential add-ons would be custom integrations with non-standard systems, advanced API usage for very high-volume operations, or white-label customization for specialized use cases. For 95% of customers, the quoted price is everything you need. We believe in clarity upfront, so there are no hidden fees or surprise charges.
externalLinks: Help Center: "What's Included in My Subscription"

faqs.question: If I create an order and then cancel it, do I still pay for that record?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, once an order is created it counts as a record even if cancelled. Use quotes for tentative loads to avoid this.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Once an order is created in the system, it does count toward your record usage, even if you later cancel or delete it. This is because the system has processed and stored that data. However, we have a workaround: use the Quotes module for tentative or unconfirmed loads. Quotes also count as records, but they're designed for this exact scenario. You can create a quote, send it to the customer, and only convert it to an order when it's confirmed. This gives you flexibility without creating unnecessary order records. Many customers use quotes as their standard workflow for all new opportunities, only converting to orders when booked.
externalLinks: Help Center: "Using Quotes to Manage Tentative Loads"

faqs.question: Does RoseRocket integrate with QuickBooks?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, RoseRocket has native QuickBooks integration with real-time bi-directional sync. Invoices, payments, and customer data sync automatically between systems.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket integrates bi-directionally with both QuickBooks Desktop and QuickBooks Online. When your team generates an invoice in RoseRocket, it automatically pushes to QuickBooks with the correct customer mapping, line items, reference numbers, and tax calculations. When payments are recorded in QuickBooks, they sync back to RoseRocket and update customer credit limits in real-time. This eliminates double entry and keeps your operations and accounting teams perfectly aligned. The integration also syncs vendor bills for carrier payments and maintains chart of accounts mapping. Setup is completed during onboarding by our implementation team and typically takes under 30 minutes. Changes reflect within minutes, giving you near real-time financial visibility.

faqs.question: Does it constantly communicate with QuickBooks?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, it's near real-time synchronization. Changes in either system reflect in the other within minutes.
faqs.detailedAnswer: The QuickBooks integration maintains constant communication between the two systems. When you mark an invoice as paid in QuickBooks, RoseRocket updates immediately, refreshing the customer's available credit. When you create an invoice in RoseRocket, it appears in QuickBooks within minutes. This real-time sync means your dispatch team always sees current credit availability when creating orders, and your accounting team never has to manually update payment records. The system handles all the background synchronization automatically, eliminating the lag time and errors that come with manual data entry or batch uploads. This is especially valuable for high-volume operations where timing matters.

faqs.question: Do you integrate with Great Plains or other accounting software?
faqs.shortAnswer: Currently we integrate with QuickBooks, Sage 50, and Xero. Great Plains is on our 2026 roadmap. For unsupported systems, we offer CSV export/import.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Our native accounting integrations currently include QuickBooks Desktop and Online, Sage 50, and Xero. These cover the majority of small to mid-sized transportation companies. For Great Plains (Dynamics GP), SAP, and NetSuite, we don't have native integrations yet, but Great Plains is actively on our product roadmap for 2026 given customer demand. In the meantime, RoseRocket offers robust CSV export capabilities for invoices, payments, and vendor bills that can be imported into any accounting system. Many customers use this workflow successfully, though it does require some manual steps. We can also discuss custom integration development for enterprise customers with specific requirements. I'd be happy to connect you with our product team to discuss timeline and priority for Great Plains.

faqs.question: Do you integrate with ELD systems like Motive or Samsara?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, RoseRocket integrates with Motive, Samsara, Geotab, and Platform Science for GPS tracking, safety events, driver scorecards, and HOS visibility.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket has native integrations with the major ELD providers including Motive (formerly KeepTruckin), Samsara, Geotab, and Platform Science. These integrations enhance visibility by syncing GPS location pings, driver HOS data, safety events like hard braking and speeding, and driver scorecards directly into RoseRocket. This allows your dispatch team to see real-time truck locations, driver availability, and accurate ETAs without leaving the TMS. Your shippers also get reliable tracking through the customer portal. The integration setup uses API tokens and typically completes in under an hour during onboarding. One note: while we do have geofencing capabilities, automatic arrival when entering a geofence is not currently available - drivers must manually click arrive. That feature is on our roadmap for 2026.

faqs.question: Can I import orders from Excel or CSV files?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, you can bulk upload via CSV, use DataBot to drag-and-drop emails/PDFs, or use TED to auto-import from your email account.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket offers three methods for importing order data. First, CSV bulk upload lets you upload spreadsheets with multiple orders - our AI auto-maps columns to RoseRocket fields, you review and adjust, then finalize. Second, DataBot is our AI email and PDF parser - just drag and drop the email or rate confirmation, and it extracts order details automatically in about 30 seconds versus 2-3 minutes for manual entry. Third, TED is our newest feature - it connects directly to your email account and automatically creates orders from incoming customer emails without any manual action. Most customers use a combination: CSV for large batch uploads, DataBot for daily order entry, and TED for regular customer emails. This flexibility means you can work the way that fits your operations best.

faqs.question: Does the mobile app have geofencing to auto-arrive drivers?
faqs.shortAnswer: RoseRocket has geofencing that notifies drivers when they enter a location, but they must manually click arrive. Auto-arrival is on our 2026 roadmap.
faqs.detailedAnswer: We do have native geofencing built into the mobile app, but it works differently than Motive's auto-arrival feature. When a driver enters the geofence around a pickup or delivery location, they receive a push notification reminding them to update their status. However, they still need to manually click the "Arrive at Task" button. We designed it this way initially to ensure accuracy - drivers confirm they're at the right location before the system updates. That said, we hear this feedback frequently, and automatic arrival upon geofence entry is actively on our product roadmap for 2026. Many of our customers coming from Motive specifically ask about this, so it's a priority. In the meantime, the notification system works well and drivers typically adapt quickly to the one-click confirmation.

faqs.question: Can data be transferred from our current TMS to RoseRocket?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, migration support is included in onboarding. We help you export from your old system, map fields, import into RoseRocket, and validate the data.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Data migration is a standard part of our onboarding process and included in your subscription. Our implementation team works with you to export data from your current system - whether that's Avaal, TMW, McLeod, or a custom homegrown platform - typically in CSV format. We then help map your existing fields to RoseRocket's data structure, import the data, and run validation checks to ensure everything transferred correctly. We commonly migrate customer databases, carrier/partner lists, driver profiles, asset information, and historical order data if needed. The process is collaborative - you maintain control over what gets migrated and when. Most migrations complete within the first two weeks of onboarding. We've successfully migrated data from dozens of different systems, so we have proven processes and templates.

faqs.question: Are there other views for dispatching besides the table view?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, RoseRocket offers both Table/List View and Timeline/Calendar View. Most customers use Timeline View for active dispatch and Table View for order management.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket provides two main dispatch views to match different workflow preferences. The Table/List View is the traditional row-by-row order listing with sortable and filterable columns - great for detailed order management and searching. The Timeline/Calendar View is our visual scheduling tool that displays orders on a timeline by date, color-coded by status, with drag-and-drop capabilities. You can group by driver, status, or date to see exactly what you need. Most of our customers use the Timeline View for active dispatch planning because it replicates the visual boards they're currently using with spreadsheets, then switch to Table View when they need to search or filter orders. Both views are fully customizable, and users can save their preferred configurations. This flexibility means dispatchers work the way that makes sense for them.

faqs.question: Can you show me what dispatch looks like with drivers listed?
faqs.shortAnswer: In Timeline View, group by "Driver" and each driver gets their own row showing all assigned loads on their timeline. Perfect for visual dispatch planning.
faqs.detailedAnswer: The Timeline View with driver grouping is exactly what you're looking for. When you group by "Driver," the system creates a row for each driver showing all their assigned loads displayed chronologically on a timeline. You can instantly see driver availability, load duration, weekly mileage, and revenue per driver. It's perfect for the visual dispatch boards many companies currently maintain with spreadsheets or whiteboards. You can drag and drop orders between drivers, see conflicts immediately when loads overlap, and quickly identify which drivers have capacity for additional loads. Colors indicate status - new, booked, in transit, delivered - so you get real-time visibility into your entire fleet at a glance. This view can be filtered by date range, division, or any custom field you create.
externalLinks: Help Center: "Grouping by Driver in Timeline View"

faqs.question: How do I combine multiple orders into one trip for a driver?
faqs.shortAnswer: Use the Manifests module to create a multi-stop trip by selecting multiple orders, or link orders by assigning the same driver - the system recognizes them as one trip.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket offers two methods for multi-order trips. Method one is creating a Manifest: go to the Manifests module, click Create Manifest, select the orders you want to combine, assign the driver and equipment, and the driver sees it as a single multi-stop trip in their mobile app with all stops in sequence. Method two is simpler for quick assignments: create your first order and assign a driver, then create your second order and assign the same driver - the system automatically recognizes this as a multi-load trip and sequences the stops appropriately. The driver app displays all pickups and deliveries in the optimal order. This flexibility works for both planned routes and ad-hoc consolidation. You can also split or modify manifests after creation if plans change.

faqs.question: Do you have features to track detention time?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, using custom formula fields. Set up a formula that calculates departure time minus arrival time to automatically track detention for billing.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Detention tracking is built into RoseRocket using our custom fields functionality. During onboarding, our implementation team sets up a custom formula field that automatically calculates detention time by subtracting the arrival timestamp from the departure timestamp. You can set thresholds for when detention charges should apply - for example, anything over 2 hours. The system calculates this automatically as drivers update their arrival and departure times in the mobile app. You can then create reports showing total detention hours per customer, detention charges owed, and which facilities consistently have the longest detention. This data can feed directly into your invoicing and also helps you identify problem facilities to address with customers. The setup takes about 15 minutes during onboarding and runs automatically from that point forward.

faqs.question: How do I split a load between two drivers?
faqs.shortAnswer: Use the Split Leg feature: open the order, click Split Leg, enter the transfer point, and assign each leg to a different driver.
faqs.detailedAnswer: The Split Leg feature is designed exactly for this scenario. Open the order, click Split Leg, and enter the middle transfer location where the handoff will happen. RoseRocket automatically creates two legs: Leg 1 from pickup to transfer point, and Leg 2 from transfer point to delivery. You then assign Driver A to Leg 1 and Driver B to Leg 2. Each driver only sees their portion of the trip in the mobile app. This is perfect for driver breakdowns, relay operations, or drop-and-hook scenarios. The system maintains the order integrity, so all documentation, tracking, and invoicing remain unified even though multiple drivers are involved. You can split legs at any time, even after a trip has started, giving you operational flexibility when things don't go according to plan.

faqs.question: Can we separate orders by division (North, South, East, West)?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, create a custom "Division" field with your options, then create separate boards filtered by each division. Users only see their division's loads.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Division separation is straightforward with RoseRocket's customization tools. First, use the Object Builder to create a custom field called "Division" with dropdown options for North, South, East, West, or whatever divisions you have. When creating orders, users select the appropriate division. Then create separate boards for each division with filters - the North board only shows orders where Division equals North. You can configure user permissions so North division users only see the North board and can't access other divisions' data. This is perfect for companies with multiple business units, regional operations, or different service lines. Each division essentially operates in their own workspace while you maintain centralized oversight and reporting across all divisions. Setup takes about 30 minutes during onboarding.

faqs.question: How easy is it to move a load from asset side to brokerage?
faqs.shortAnswer: If same company entity: very easy, just change driver assignment to carrier. If separate companies: requires manual recreation in the other account.
faqs.detailedAnswer: This depends on how your asset and brokerage operations are structured. If you're running both under the same company entity with the same MC number, it's very easy - you simply change the assignment from a driver to a carrier partner within the same order. Everything stays in one RoseRocket instance. However, if your asset and brokerage are separate legal entities with different MC numbers, you'll need two separate RoseRocket subscriptions, and moving a load requires manually recreating the order in the other account. There's a workaround where you can copy the order details and paste them into a new order to speed this up. Our recommendation: if you frequently move loads between asset and brokerage, structure them as divisions within a single company entity rather than separate subscriptions. This gives you full flexibility to reassign loads with one click.
externalLinks: Help Center: "Managing Asset and Brokerage Operations"

faqs.question: Can I track loaded vs empty trailers?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, RoseRocket's asset management shows which trailers are assigned to active loads versus available, with optional GPS location tracking.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket includes asset management features specifically for tracking equipment utilization. The system automatically tracks which trailers are assigned to active trips (loaded) versus unassigned and available (empty). If you have GPS tracking on your trailers through an integrated system, you can also see real-time location. You can create a custom dashboard widget showing total trailers, loaded count, empty count, and out-of-service equipment. This gives you instant visibility into asset utilization and helps with equipment planning. You can also set alerts for trailers that have been sitting empty at customer locations beyond a certain threshold. The asset module integrates with your dispatch workflow, so trailers automatically update status as they're assigned to and removed from loads.

faqs.question: Can I see how many miles a driver is running per week?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, view in driver profiles with timeframe filters, add a mileage column to Manifests board grouped by driver, or use driver performance reports.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Driver mileage tracking is available in multiple places within RoseRocket. The driver profile shows total miles with filters for any timeframe - you can view current week, month, quarter, or custom date ranges. In the Manifests board, add a "Total Miles" column and group by driver to see weekly mileage for all drivers at once. There's also a dedicated driver performance report that breaks down miles, revenue, and trip counts by driver over any period. If you use the Timeline View grouped by driver, you can visually see their weekly schedule and associated mileage. This data is useful for driver pay calculations, utilization analysis, and balancing workload across your fleet. The mileage calculations are automatic based on the routes in each order, or you can manually override if needed.

faqs.question: Are drivers using a mobile app for capturing POD?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, RoseRocket has a native iOS and Android mobile app. Drivers can scan documents, capture digital signatures, take photos, or upload from their gallery.
faqs.detailedAnswer: The RoseRocket mobile app is purpose-built for drivers and available on both iOS and Android. For POD capture, drivers have four options: scan documents using the camera which auto-crops and creates a PDF, capture digital signatures directly on screen, take photos of freight or damage, or upload images from their gallery if they took photos earlier. The scan feature works great for multi-page BOLs - drivers can scan multiple pages in sequence and it compiles them into one PDF. All captured PODs automatically sync to the order in real-time and appear in the documents tab where your office team can access them immediately. This eliminates the old workflow of drivers texting photos or dropping off paperwork. The app is intuitive enough that most drivers are comfortable using it within a day or two of training.

faqs.question: Can drivers use their own phones or do we need to provide tablets?
faqs.shortAnswer: Drivers can use their personal phones. The app works on iPhone (iOS 12+) and Android (8+). Tablets work too if you prefer larger screens for signatures.
faqs.detailedAnswer: One of the benefits of RoseRocket is that drivers can use their personal smartphones - no need to purchase devices. The app is compatible with iPhone running iOS 12 or newer and Android phones running version 8 or newer, which covers virtually all phones from the last 5-6 years. If you prefer larger screens for signature capture, tablets work great too, both iOS and Android. The app is very lightweight and uses minimal data - typically around 50MB per month for regular usage. Most companies have their drivers use personal phones, which eliminates device management headaches and reduces costs. Drivers generally prefer this too since they're already comfortable with their own devices. There's no limit on the number of driver users, so you can have as many drivers as needed without additional fees.

faqs.question: When a driver arrives in a geofence, does it automatically arrive them?
faqs.shortAnswer: No, not automatically currently. Drivers get a notification when entering the geofence but must manually click arrive. Auto-arrival is on our 2026 roadmap.
faqs.detailedAnswer: This is a common question, especially from companies using Motive. RoseRocket does have geofencing built into the mobile app, but it works differently than auto-arrival. When a driver enters the geofenced area around a pickup or delivery location, they receive a push notification reminding them to update their status. They then manually click the "Arrive at Task" button to confirm. We designed it this way initially to ensure accuracy - drivers confirm they're at the correct location before the system updates customer- facing tracking. However, we hear this feedback frequently, and automatic arrival when entering a geofence is actively prioritized on our 2026 product roadmap. In the meantime, the notification system works well and most drivers adapt quickly to the one-click confirmation. It's worth noting that the majority of TMS systems don't have auto-arrival yet - Motive is somewhat unique in this feature.

faqs.question: Does the mobile app work offline?
faqs.shortAnswer: Partial offline capability: drivers can view loaded trip details offline, but need connectivity to update status. POD photos queue and upload when back online.
faqs.detailedAnswer: The mobile app has partial offline functionality. Drivers can view all the details of their assigned trips when offline - pickup and delivery addresses, contact information, special instructions, and load details. However, they do need cellular or WiFi connectivity to update statuses like arrived, departed, or completed. If they capture POD photos or signatures while offline, those queue locally on the device and automatically upload as soon as they regain connectivity. This design ensures data integrity and prevents sync conflicts. For most drivers, this works well since they have connectivity at customer locations. If you have routes through areas with poor cell coverage, drivers can download their trip information before departing and then sync updates when back in range. Full offline capability with local database syncing is something we're exploring for future releases.

faqs.question: Can the mobile app be used in multiple languages?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, the mobile app supports English, Spanish, and French. Drivers can select their preferred language in app settings.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Language support is built directly into the RoseRocket mobile app. Drivers can choose from English, Spanish, or French as their display language in the app settings. This is particularly valuable for diverse driver populations where not everyone is comfortable with English. The entire app interface, buttons, labels, and instructions translate to the selected language. This improves driver adoption and reduces training time since drivers can work in their native language. Each driver sets their own preference independently, so different drivers on the same account can use different languages. The language selection persists even after app updates. If you need additional languages beyond these three, we can discuss custom translation options for enterprise customers.

faqs.question: Can I create custom fields for my specific business needs?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, using Object Builder you can create unlimited custom fields - text, number, money, date, dropdown, checkbox, or formula fields. No coding required.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket's Object Builder gives you complete control over customization without any coding. You can create custom fields for any object in the system - orders, customers, carriers, drivers, assets. The process is simple: go to Settings, click Object Builder, choose where you want to add a field, then select the field type: text for general information, number for quantities, money for pricing, date for timestamps, dropdown for predefined choices, checkbox for yes/no options, or formula for calculated fields. The field is immediately available across the system. Common examples include rally program numbers, company-specific pro bill formats, commodity subtypes, division codes, and custom reference numbers. These custom fields are fully integrated - they're searchable, filterable, and can be included on reports and documents. This flexibility means the 20% of unique needs specific to your business can be configured without expensive custom development.

faqs.question: What sort of custom fields are other carriers adding?
faqs.shortAnswer: Common custom fields include commodity details, reference numbers, division tracking, customer-specific codes, regulatory permits, and detention tracking fields.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Based on our customer base, the most common custom fields fall into several categories. For commodity tracking: dry bulk vs liquid bulk, specialized materials, product codes. For operational needs: company-specific tracking numbers, division or region codes, equipment type requirements. For customer requirements: PO numbers, job site codes, project identifiers, gate codes. For regulatory compliance: permit numbers, special handling codes, hazmat classifications. For billing: detention start/end times, accessorial codes, fuel surcharge calculations. Bulk carriers often create fields for tonnage, material density, or temperature requirements. LTL operations add freight class, NMFC codes, and stackability flags. The beautiful part is that RoseRocket handles about 80% of needs out-of-box, so these custom fields truly address your unique 20%. During onboarding, we review your current processes and recommend which custom fields would add value.

faqs.question: Can I customize the invoice, BOL, and other documents?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, all documents are fully customizable: invoices, BOLs, rate confirmations, PODs, and pay stubs. Customization happens during onboarding with our support team.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Document customization is a standard part of RoseRocket implementation. You can fully customize the format and layout of invoices, bills of lading, rate confirmations, proof of delivery documents, and driver pay stubs. This includes adding your company logo, adjusting which fields appear and where, incorporating any custom fields you've created, modifying the layout to match your brand, and adjusting formatting for specific customer requirements. Our implementation team handles the technical configuration during onboarding based on your requirements and examples of your current documents. Most customers bring us their existing templates, and we replicate the look and feel in RoseRocket. The customized documents then generate automatically from your data, maintaining consistency across all customer interactions. If you need changes after go-live, your account manager can coordinate updates with our support team.

faqs.question: Can all this be pre-configured for non-technical staff?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, absolutely. Our implementation team pre-configures everything during onboarding. Users get simplified views based on their role and only see what they need.
faqs.detailedAnswer: This is a major focus area for us because we hear this concern frequently. During onboarding, our implementation team works closely with you to pre-configure boards, views, fields, and workflows based on each team member's role. Dispatch users get a streamlined view with only the modules and fields they need for daily work - no overwhelming options. Accounting users see their relevant financial modules. Non-technical staff receive simplified interfaces that guide them through processes step-by-step. We heard from one of your peers: "I know we've got a lot of people on our team that aren't very advanced with computers." This is incredibly common, and our onboarding process specifically addresses it through role-based simplification. Users don't need to configure anything themselves - they log in and see exactly what they need to do their job. Admin users retain full access to make future adjustments, but frontline users experience a tailored, straightforward system.
externalLinks: Help Center: "Getting Started for Non-Technical Users"

faqs.question: Can I set up multiple divisions on separate boards?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, create a custom Division field, then create filtered boards for each division. Users only see their assigned division's data.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Division separation is straightforward and commonly configured during onboarding. First, we create a custom field called Division with dropdown options for your divisions - North, South, East, West, or whatever structure you use. Then we create separate boards for each division with filters that only show orders matching that division. We can configure user permissions so North division users only have access to the North board and can't see other divisions' orders. This creates functional separation while maintaining centralized data and reporting at the management level. It's perfect for regional operations, multiple business units, or different service lines like asset vs brokerage. Each division essentially operates independently while you maintain enterprise visibility. You can also create combined views for managers who need to see across divisions. The entire setup takes about 30 minutes during onboarding and scales to as many divisions as you need.

faqs.question: Does this work for each individual user that logs in?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, each user can have personalized boards, views, column configurations, and filters. They can duplicate shared boards and customize them without affecting others.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket provides complete user-level customization. Each person who logs in can have their own personal boards and views, individual column configurations, saved filters and searches, and personal dashboards. There are two approaches: shared boards where changes affect all users with access, and personal boards where a user duplicates a shared board and customizes it for themselves - only they can see their version. This is important because different users have different workflows. Your dispatch supervisor might want to see columns organized one way, while a dispatcher prefers a different layout. One user might group orders by status while another groups by customer. Everyone can work their own way without conflicting with others. The best practice we recommend is giving users personal boards so they can organize their workspace to match how their brain works. This increases adoption and efficiency.

faqs.question: Is there a way to only show specific modules to dispatch users?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, role-based module access lets you control which modules each role sees. Dispatch might only see Orders and Drivers, while Accounting sees financial modules.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Role-based module access is a core feature that prevents user overwhelm. As an administrator, you configure which modules each role can see in the left sidebar. For example, dispatch users might only see Orders, Manifests, Drivers, and Assets - the operational modules they need daily. Accounting users would see Invoices, Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable, and Payroll - their financial modules. Operations managers might see everything for full visibility. This dramatically simplifies the interface for frontline users. Instead of a sidebar with 15 modules they don't understand, they see only 4-5 relevant to their job. This reduces training time, prevents errors from users accessing areas they shouldn't, and makes the system feel less overwhelming. You can create as many roles as needed and adjust module access anytime. This configuration happens during onboarding as part of our role-based setup process.

faqs.question: Does everybody have access to customer credit terms and sensitive info?
faqs.shortAnswer: No, you have field-level access control. Set fields to full access, read-only, or hidden based on user role. Dispatch might see customer names but not credit terms.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket provides granular field-level permissions in addition to module access. For any field in the system - whether built-in or custom - you can configure three access levels by role: full access for read and write, read- only for viewing but not editing, or hidden for no visibility at all. A common configuration: dispatch users can see customer names and contact information but credit terms are hidden. Accounting users can see and edit all financial fields including credit limits and payment terms. Sales users might see available credit to know if they can book more orders, but can't change credit limits. This protects sensitive information while ensuring people have the data they need for their jobs. You can get as granular as needed - some customers even hide specific custom fields from certain users. These permissions are set during onboarding and can be adjusted anytime as roles evolve.

faqs.question: Can users only see orders for their division/region?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, using Security Filters on boards. East division users would only see East orders and cannot access orders outside their filter.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Security Filters provide data-level access control beyond just module and field permissions. You can configure boards with filters that restrict which records users can see based on criteria like division, region, customer type, or any field in the system. For example, create an East division board with a security filter where Division equals East. Users assigned to that board can only see and interact with East orders - they cannot search for or access orders from other divisions even if they try. This creates true data separation while everyone works in the same system. It's perfect for regional operations, commission-based sales territories, or multi-branch companies where you need division of responsibility. Managers can have access to multiple filtered boards to see across divisions, while frontline users stay within their scope. Security filters are configured during onboarding by our implementation team as part of your permission structure.

faqs.question: Can users duplicate a shared board for personal customization?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, any user can duplicate a shared board, name it (like "Joe's Orders"), customize it, and only they and admins can see their version.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Board duplication is designed to give users personal customization freedom. Any user can take a shared board, click Duplicate Board, give it a personal name like "Joe's Orders View" or "My Dispatch Board," and then make whatever customizations they want - add columns, change grouping, adjust filters, modify colors. Only that user and system administrators can see their personal board. The original shared board remains unchanged for everyone else. This is valuable because one dispatcher might want orders grouped by status while another prefers grouping by customer. One person might want profitability visible while another focuses on ETA. Everyone gets the exact view they need without forcing everyone into the same layout. Users can create multiple personal boards for different purposes - one for active dispatch, one for delivered loads, one for problem orders. This flexibility dramatically improves user satisfaction and productivity.

faqs.question: How long does onboarding take?
faqs.shortAnswer: Standard timeline is 60-90 days with a 3-month activation period. Fast-track option available in 30 days for motivated teams. You can start using the system while training.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket onboarding typically follows a 60-90 day timeline, though we offer flexibility based on your needs and urgency. The structure includes: weeks 1-2 for account setup, data migration, and initial configuration; weeks 3-4 for user training and workflow customization; weeks 5-8 for parallel system testing where you run both your old and new systems; and weeks 9-12 for full cutover and optimization. For highly motivated teams with simpler operations, we offer a fast-track option that can complete in 30 days. The key advantage is you can start using RoseRocket immediately while training continues - many customers run both systems in parallel during transition to ensure smooth handoff. You're assigned a dedicated implementation specialist who conducts weekly calls and provides comprehensive support throughout. The 3-month activation period ensures adequate time for your team to become proficient before committing to the 12-month contract.
externalLinks: Help Center: "What to Expect During Onboarding"

faqs.question: Can we use RoseRocket while our team is still learning it?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes! Start with pilot users, run parallel with your current system, and gradually transition teams. Full support is provided during the transition.
faqs.detailedAnswer: This is not only possible but actually our recommended approach. Most successful implementations start with a pilot group - typically 2-3 dispatchers or a single division. They begin creating orders and working in RoseRocket while the rest of the team continues with your current system. As the pilot users gain confidence and you validate workflows, you gradually expand to additional teams. Many customers run both systems completely in parallel for 30-60 days, entering the same orders in both places, to ensure nothing falls through the cracks. This phased approach reduces risk and allows learning without pressure. You have full support from your implementation specialist during this entire period - weekly calls, ad-hoc questions, and access to training materials. The best practice is starting with your dispatch team since they're creating orders, then expanding to accounting and other departments once dispatch is comfortable.

faqs.question: What support is included during onboarding?
faqs.shortAnswer: You get a dedicated implementation team, data migration assistance, system configuration, user training, ongoing support via email/phone/chat, knowledge base access, and an account manager.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket onboarding includes comprehensive support at no additional cost. You're assigned a dedicated implementation specialist who becomes your primary contact throughout the process. They conduct weekly video calls to track progress and address questions. Data migration assistance includes helping you export from your current system, mapping fields, importing into RoseRocket, and validation. System configuration covers all the setup: custom fields, boards, permissions, document templates, and integrations. User training includes both live sessions and recorded modules your team can reference anytime. You also get ongoing support through email, phone, and live chat with our support team. The knowledge base and help center provide self-service documentation and tutorials. After go-live, your account manager remains your long-term contact for questions, best practices, and optimization. This comprehensive support model ensures you're never left figuring things out alone.

faqs.question: Can you migrate our data for us?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, data migration support is included. We help you export from your current system, map fields, import into RoseRocket, and validate everything transferred correctly.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Data migration is a standard component of RoseRocket onboarding, included in your subscription. Our implementation team guides the entire process. First, we help you export data from your current system - whether that's Avaal, TMW, McLeod, or a custom platform - typically in CSV format. We then work together to map your existing field structure to RoseRocket's data model. Common migrations include customer databases with contact and credit information, carrier and partner lists, driver profiles with credentials and contact details, asset and equipment inventories, and optionally historical order data if you need it for reference. We import the data, run validation checks to ensure accuracy, and work with you to clean up any issues. The process is collaborative - you maintain control over what gets migrated and timing. Most data migrations complete within the first two weeks of onboarding. We've successfully migrated data from dozens of different systems and have proven templates and processes.

faqs.question: How can I get profitability margin for each load?
faqs.shortAnswer: Built-in profitability tracking shows revenue minus all costs (carrier pay, driver pay, fuel, accessorials) in real-time on each order and in reports.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket calculates profitability automatically by tracking revenue and all associated costs. Revenue comes from your customer invoice amount. Costs include carrier or partner payments, driver pay, fuel surcharges, detention, and any other accessorials you add. The system calculates margin as revenue minus costs and displays it in multiple places: directly on the individual order screen as you're working, in dedicated profitability reports you can filter by customer or date range, on the order list board by adding a margin column and percentage column, and in dashboard widgets for at-a-glance visibility. The calculations update in real-time as costs are added to orders, so you always have current margin data. This helps with quick decision-making on whether to accept loads, pricing negotiations, and identifying which customers and lanes are most profitable. You can also create margin-based alerts if loads fall below your target thresholds.

faqs.question: Is there live tracking that customers can see?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes. Generate shareable links for individual orders or create customer portal boards. Customers see real-time GPS, status updates, and ETAs without logging in.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket provides two options for customer visibility. Option one is single order sharing: generate a unique shareable link for any order and email it to your customer. They click the link without needing login credentials and see real-time GPS location via your ELD integration, current pickup/delivery status, updated ETA, and all order details you choose to share. Option two is customer portal boards: create a board filtered for a specific customer showing all their loads, share a permanent link they can bookmark, and it updates in real-time as status changes. This significantly reduces "where's my truck" calls to your operations team. You maintain complete control over what information customers can see - some companies share everything, others only show high-level status. The tracking pages are mobile-responsive so customers can check from their phones. This transparency improves customer satisfaction and differentiates your service.

faqs.question: Do you have a dashboard to track loaded vs empty trailers?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, asset management shows which trailers are assigned to active loads versus available. Create custom dashboard widgets showing total, loaded, empty, and out-of-service counts.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket's asset management module provides complete visibility into equipment utilization. The system automatically tracks which trailers are currently assigned to active trips - these show as loaded. Unassigned trailers show as available or empty. If you have GPS tracking integrated on your trailers, you can also see real-time location on a map. You can create custom dashboard widgets displaying total trailer count, loaded count with percentage, empty count with percentage, and out-of-service equipment that needs maintenance. This dashboard gives you instant visibility into asset utilization and helps with equipment planning. You can also set automated alerts for trailers sitting empty at customer locations beyond a certain threshold - for example, notify you if a trailer has been at a customer site for more than 48 hours. The asset module integrates seamlessly with dispatch, so trailer status updates automatically as they're assigned to and removed from loads.

faqs.question: Can I see how many miles a driver is running per week?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, view driver mileage in driver profiles with timeframe filters, add mileage columns to boards grouped by driver, or use driver performance reports.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Driver mileage visibility is built into multiple areas of RoseRocket. In the driver profile, you can view total miles with flexible timeframe filters - current week, month, quarter, year-to-date, or custom date ranges. This historical view helps with compensation planning and utilization analysis. In the Manifests board, add a "Total Miles" column and group by driver to see a side-by-side comparison of weekly mileage across your entire driver fleet. There's also a dedicated driver performance report that breaks down miles, revenue, number of trips, and average miles per trip by driver over any period you specify. If you use Timeline View grouped by driver, you can visually see each driver's schedule and the mileage associated with each load. Mileage calculations are automatic based on the routes in each order, or you can manually override if needed. This data supports driver pay calculations, helps balance workload fairly across your fleet, and identifies utilization opportunities.

faqs.question: Is there a history of changes showing who made that change?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, complete audit trail. Every change is logged with the user who made it, date and time, and before/after values. View in the Activity panel on each order.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket maintains a comprehensive audit trail for accountability and transparency. Every change made to an order - or any other record in the system - is logged with the specific user who made the change, exact date and timestamp, and what was changed including before and after values. This appears in the Activity panel on each order, showing a chronological history of all modifications. You can see who changed the rate, who reassigned the driver, who updated the status, who added accessorial charges - everything. This creates complete accountability and eliminates "I never changed that" situations. As one customer put it: "So nobody can say they never changed something - we know exactly who did." Managers love this feature for accountability and training purposes. It's also valuable for resolving customer disputes when you can show exactly when and who updated information. The audit log is permanent and cannot be edited or deleted, ensuring data integrity.
externalLinks: Help Center: "Viewing Change History and Audit Logs"

faqs.question: So nobody can say they never changed something?
faqs.shortAnswer: Correct. Every edit is permanently tracked with user, timestamp, and before/after values. Complete transparency equals accountability.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Exactly - that's the entire purpose of the audit trail. Every single edit made in the system is permanently logged and cannot be altered or deleted. If someone changes a rate, reassigns a driver, updates delivery status, modifies a customer address, or makes any other change, it's recorded with their user account, the exact date and time, and what the values were before and after the change. This creates ironclad accountability. You can pull up any order and see the complete history of modifications. This is particularly valuable when investigating errors, resolving customer complaints, or managing employee performance. If there's a dispute about when information was updated or who made a mistake, the audit log provides definitive answers. The transparency also tends to improve accuracy because users know their actions are tracked. As you mentioned, managers love this feature while workers are sometimes less enthusiastic, but ultimately it creates a culture of accountability and accuracy that benefits everyone.

faqs.question: Do you track detention time?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, using custom formula fields that automatically calculate departure time minus arrival time. Can set billing thresholds and generate detention reports.
faqs.detailedAnswer: Detention time tracking is configured during onboarding using RoseRocket's custom formula fields. We create a field that automatically calculates the difference between when a driver marks arrived and when they mark departed at each stop. You can set thresholds - for example, anything over 2 hours triggers detention charges. As drivers update their arrival and departure times via the mobile app, the system calculates detention automatically in real-time. You can then create reports showing total detention hours by customer, total detention charges owed, and which facilities consistently have the longest detention times. This data feeds directly into your invoicing workflow, so detention charges can be added to customer invoices automatically. It's also valuable for operational analysis - identifying problem facilities, negotiating better terms with chronic offenders, and planning routes to avoid high-detention locations. The entire setup takes about 15 minutes during onboarding and then runs automatically forever.
externalLinks: Help Center: "Tracking and Billing Detention Time"

faqs.question: Can we share information with brokers or carriers?
faqs.shortAnswer: Yes, two methods: generate single-order shareable links for specific loads, or create permanent filtered boards that partners can bookmark to see all their current loads.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket provides flexible sharing capabilities for external partners. Method one is single order links: click "Share Link" on any order, send the unique URL to your broker or carrier, and they can view order details you've chosen to share without needing to log in. You control what's visible - full details, limited information, or specific fields. Method two is shared boards: create a board filtered for a specific partner showing all loads you're hauling for them or they're hauling for you, generate a permanent shareable link, and they bookmark it for ongoing access. The board updates in real-time as new loads are added or statuses change. This is perfect for brokers you work with regularly who want visibility into all their loads with you. The access is read-only - partners can't edit anything - and you can revoke access anytime. This eliminates constant "what's the status" phone calls and emails, improving efficiency for both parties.
externalLinks: Help Center: "Sharing with Brokers and Carriers"

faqs.question: Would this be a separate web link or combined in the main portal?
faqs.shortAnswer: It's a separate shareable link. Partners receive a unique URL, not tied to your main portal. Read-only access that can be revoked anytime.
faqs.detailedAnswer: When you share information with external partners, they receive a unique URL that's completely separate from your main RoseRocket portal login. The link provides read-only access to only the specific information you've chosen to share - either a single order or a filtered board of their loads. They don't get access to your overall system, can't see other customers' data, and can't make any edits. The link works without requiring them to create an account or log in, making it extremely simple for partners to access. You maintain complete control - you can revoke access to the link at any time if your relationship with that partner ends. For customers who use shared boards, they typically bookmark the URL and check it whenever they need status updates, rather than calling or emailing you. This separate link approach provides secure, controlled access without giving external parties any deeper access to your system.
externalLinks: Help Center: "How External Sharing Links Work"

faqs.question: Can customers see their invoices online?
faqs.shortAnswer: Not directly through RoseRocket currently. Workarounds include auto-emailing invoices via QuickBooks, sharing boards with invoice status, or using QuickBooks customer portal.
faqs.detailedAnswer: RoseRocket doesn't currently have a direct customer-facing invoice portal where customers can log in and view their billing history. However, there are several effective workarounds. Most commonly, customers configure their QuickBooks integration to automatically email invoices to customers as PDFs when generated - this is the standard approach most companies use. Alternatively, you can create a shared board that shows a customer all their orders along with invoice status (invoiced, paid, outstanding) - they can't view the actual invoice document, but they see what's been billed and payment status. If you use QuickBooks Online, you can leverage QuickBooks' native customer portal where customers log in directly to view and pay invoices. Some customers also use third-party accounts receivable portals that integrate with QuickBooks. A native customer invoice portal is something we're evaluating for future releases based on customer feedback, so it may be added to the product roadmap.
